name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q01 - Incorrect statement regarding human fertilization and implantation

questiontext.text: Choose the incorrect statement from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fertilisation and embryonic development in amniotes involve specific adaptations including internal syngamy, nourishment via maternal secretions, regulated blocks to polyspermy, and precise timing of blastocyst implantation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Internal Fertilisation
In terrestrial vertebrates including birds and mammals, syngamy of gametes occurs inside the body of the female reproductive tract to protect the gametes from desiccation and facilitate successful union. Hence, internal fertilisation takes place in both birds and mammals.

Step 3: Evaluation of Colostrum Composition
The initial milk produced by maternal mammary glands during the early days of lactation is colostrum. It is abundant in proteins, minerals, and maternal antibodies, predominantly secretory immunoglobulin A, providing essential nutrients and systemic passive immunity to the newborn.

Step 4: Evaluation of Implantation Timing
Following fertilisation in the ampulla of the fallopian tube, the cleavage divisions produce a blastocyst that travels into the uterine cavity. Implantation of the blastocyst into the uterine endometrium typically occurs approximately seven days post-fertilisation.

Step 5: Evaluation of Polyspermy Prevention Mechanism
In mammals, the block to polyspermy is triggered when a fertilising spermatozoon binds to sperm receptors on the zona pellucida. This induces the cortical reaction, in which cortical granules exocytose enzymes into the perivitelline space, altering the glycoproteins of the extracellular zona pellucida and hardening it against further sperm entry. It is not mediated by chemical modifications on the egg plasma membrane surface itself. Therefore, the statement stating that polyspermy is prevented by chemical changes in the egg surface is biologically inaccurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conclusion
The inaccurate statement describes the block to polyspermy as being caused by chemical changes of the egg surface rather than modifications of the zona pellucida.
Final Answer: Polyspermy in mammals is prevented by the chemical changes in the egg surface

answer.text: In birds and mammals internal fertilisation takes place
Polyspermy in mammals is prevented by the chemical changes in the egg surface
In the human female implantation occurs almost seven days after fertilisation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q02 - Hormone levels and cellular events during menstrual cycle

questiontext.text: Identify the correct statement from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The human ovarian and uterine cycles are governed by cyclic changes in pituitary gonadotropins and ovarian steroid hormones, alongside distinct gametogenic timelines in males and females.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Ovulatory Trigger
The ovulatory surge refers specifically to the abrupt mid-cycle peak in luteinizing hormone from the anterior pituitary gland, which directly induces the rupture of the mature follicle and release of the secondary oocyte. While high levels of estrogen exert positive feedback on the pituitary, the ovulatory surge itself is composed of luteinizing hormone.

Step 3: Evaluation of Oogonial Formation Timeline
In human females, oogenesis initiates during embryonic development. All oogonia (gamete mother cells) multiply by mitosis in the fetal ovary prior to birth, forming a finite pool of primary oocytes. No additional oogonia are formed or proliferate after birth or from puberty onwards.

Step 4: Evaluation of Sperm Motility upon Release
Spermatozoa released into the lumen of seminiferous tubules via spermiation are immotile or sluggishly motile. They attain progressive motility and fertilization capacity subsequently during transit and maturation through the epididymis.

Step 5: Evaluation of Post-Ovulatory Hormone Levels
Following ovulation, the remnants of the ruptured Graafian follicle luteinize to form the corpus luteum under the influence of luteinizing hormone. The corpus luteum functions as a temporary endocrine gland, synthesizing and secreting large quantities of progesterone to prepare and maintain the secretory endometrium for potential implantation. Hence, progesterone levels are markedly elevated during the post-ovulatory (luteal) phase.

Step 6: Check and Final Conclusion
Among the statements, the accurate description is that progesterone levels remain elevated during the post-ovulatory phase of the menstrual cycle.
Final Answer: Progesterone level is high during the post ovulatory phase of menstrual cycle.

answer.text: High levels of estrogen triggers the ovulatory surge.
Oogonial cells start to proliferate and give rise to functional ova in regular cycles from puberty onwards.
Sperms released from seminiferous tubules are highly motile.
Progesterone level is high during the post ovulatory phase of menstrual cycle.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q03 - Odd structure with reference to male reproductive system

questiontext.text: Spot the odd one out from the following structures with reference to the male reproductive system:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The human reproductive tracts consist of distinct sex-specific primary organs, accessory duct systems, and external genitalia.

Step 2: Evaluation of Male Duct Structures
The male reproductive accessory ducts include the rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, and vas deferens. The rete testis forms an interconnected network of tubules within the mediastinum testis; the vasa efferentia carry spermatozoa from the rete testis to the highly coiled epididymis, where sperms are stored and mature.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Female Duct Structure
The isthmus is the narrow, thick-walled terminal segment of the female Fallopian tube (oviduct) that connects the ampulla directly to the uterine cavity. It is an anatomical component of the female reproductive system.

Step 4: Check and Final Conclusion
Because the rete testis, epididymis, and vasa efferentia belong to the male reproductive duct system while the isthmus belongs to the female reproductive tract, the isthmus is the odd structure.
Final Answer: Isthmus

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q04 - Glands contributing fluid part of seminal plasma

questiontext.text:
Seminal plasma, the fluid part of semen, is contributed by.

i. Seminal vesicle
ii. Prostate gland
iii. Urethra
iv. Bulbourethral gland

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Semen is a composite fluid consisting of suspended spermatozoa and seminal plasma, which is the collective fluid vehicle synthesized by male accessory sex glands.

Step 2: Analysis of Contributing Glands
The male accessory glands comprise paired seminal vesicles, a single prostate gland, and paired bulbourethral glands. The seminal vesicles produce a viscous, alkaline secretion rich in fructose, ascorbic acid, and prostaglandins. The prostate gland contributes a milky, slightly acidic fluid containing citrate, acid phosphatase, and proteolytic enzymes. The bulbourethral glands produce clear, alkaline mucus that provides lubrication and neutralizes residual urinary acidity in the urethra.

Step 3: Role of the Urethra
The urethra serves as an excretory and reproductive conduit that conveys urine and semen out of the body. It does not synthesize or secrete fluid contributing to the bulk volume of seminal plasma.

Step 4: Check and Final Conclusion
Seminal plasma is therefore formed by the combined secretions of the seminal vesicle, prostate gland, and bulbourethral gland, which corresponds to items i, ii, and iv.
Final Answer: i, ii and iv

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q05 - Process of release of sperms in spermiation

questiontext.text: Spermiation is the process of the release of sperms from:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Spermatogenesis comprises successive cellular differentiations including the proliferation of spermatogonia, meiotic division of spermatocytes into spermatids, morphological transformation into spermatozoa (spermiogenesis), and liberation of spermatozoa into the tubular lumen.

Step 2: Definition and Site of Spermiation
During spermiogenesis, non-motile circular spermatids transform into elongated spermatozoa. The heads of these developing spermatozoa remain embedded within supporting Sertoli cells to derive nourishment. The final detachment and release of mature spermatozoa from the Sertoli cells into the central lumen of the seminiferous tubules is designated as spermiation.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
Spermiation is strictly the release of sperms from the seminiferous tubules into the ductal lumen.
Final Answer: Seminiferous tubules

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q06 - Presence of mature Graafian follicle in menstrual cycle

questiontext.text: Mature Graafian follicle is generally present in the ovary of a healthy human female around:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The follicular phase of a typical 28-day human menstrual cycle features the progressive maturation of primary follicles into tertiary and fully mature pre-ovulatory Graafian follicles under the control of follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone.

Step 2: Chronological Sequence of Follicular Growth
Following menstruation (days 1 to 5), several primary follicles begin growth during days 5 to 10. A single dominant tertiary follicle is selected and enlarges significantly, accumulating follicular fluid within the antrum to form the mature Graafian follicle. This fully developed state is reached between days 11 and 14, culminating in ovulation around day 14 when stimulated by the surge in luteinizing hormone. Thus, the mature follicle persists in the ovary within the window of days 11 to 17.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
In a regular female cycle, the mature Graafian follicle is typically present during days 11 to 17.
Final Answer: 11 – 17 day of menstrual cycle

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q07 - Contact inducing acrosomal reaction in sperm

questiontext.text: Acrosomal reaction of the sperm occurs due to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fertilisation requires a sequence of physiological adaptations by the spermatozoon, including capacitation within the female genital tract followed by the acrosome reaction upon reaching the ovum.

Step 2: Induction of the Acrosome Reaction
When a capacitated sperm traverses the corona radiata and establishes physical contact with the zona pellucida of the ovum, specific sperm surface proteins bind to glycoprotein receptors (such as ZP3) on the zona pellucida. This receptor-ligand interaction triggers an influx of calcium ions into the sperm head, inducing the exocytosis of acrosomal enzymes (hyaluronidase, corona penetrating enzyme, and acrosin) that lyse the egg coatings.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The acrosomal reaction is specifically initiated by contact of the sperm with the zona pellucida of the ovum.
Final Answer: Its contact with zona pellucida of the ova

answer.text: Its contact with zona pellucida of the ova
Reactions within the uterine environment of the female
Reactions within the epididymal environment of the male

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q08 - Identification of non accessory gland in male system

questiontext.text: Which one of the following is not a male accessory gland?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The male reproductive system consists of primary sex organs (testes), accessory ducts, accessory glands, and external genitalia.

Step 2: Classification of Structures
The male accessory sex glands are three in kind: paired seminal vesicles, an unpaired prostate gland, and paired bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands. In contrast, an ampulla is an anatomical enlargement or dilatation of a duct, such as the swollen terminal reservoir of the vas deferens before it joins the seminal vesicle duct, or the widest part of the oviduct. It is an accessory duct segment rather than a secretory gland.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
Among the listed structures, the ampulla is a ductal dilatation and not an accessory gland.
Final Answer: Ampulla

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q09 - Division and ploidy during stages of spermatogenesis

questiontext.text: The spermatogonia undergo division to produce sperms by the process of spermatogenesis. Choose the correct one with reference to above.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Spermatogenesis involves sequential mitotic multiplication, reductional meiosis I, and equational meiosis II to produce haploid male gametes from diploid stem cells.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cell Divisions and Ploidy
Spermatogonia possess 46 chromosomes (diploid, 2n) and divide by mitosis to maintain stem cell populations or generate primary spermatocytes; they do not undergo meiosis directly.
Primary spermatocytes (diploid, 2n = 46) undergo the first meiotic division (a reductional division), not mitosis, yielding two equal haploid secondary spermatocytes.
Secondary spermatocytes possess 23 chromosomes (haploid, n = 23) and proceed through the second meiotic division (equational division) to form four haploid spermatids.
Spermatids are subsequently converted into mature spermatozoa through spermiogenesis, not the reverse.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The biologically correct statement confirms that secondary spermatocytes have 23 chromosomes and undergo the second meiotic division.
Final Answer: Secondary spermatocytes have 23 chromosomes and undergo second meiotic division

answer.text: Spermatogonia have 46 chromosomes and always undergo meiotic cell division
Primary spermatocytes divide by mitotic cell division
Secondary spermatocytes have 23 chromosomes and undergo second meiotic division

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q10 - Match parts of sperm with their functions

questiontext.text:
Match between the following representing parts of the sperm and their functions and choose the correct option.

Column IColumn II
A. Headi. Enzymes
B. Middle pieceii. Sperm motility
C. Acrosomeiii. Energy
D. Tailiv. Genetic material

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A microscopic mammalian spermatozoon is composed of four distinct functional regions: head, neck, middle piece, and tail, each specialized for delivering paternal genes to the ovum.

Step 2: Matching Analysis
Head: Encloses an elongated haploid nucleus carrying condensed chromosomal DNA, matching with genetic material.
Middle piece: Contains numerous spirally coiled mitochondria surrounding the axial filament that synthesize ATP, providing energy for propulsion.
Acrosome: An anterior lysosome-derived cap filled with proteolytic and hydrolytic enzymes necessary for dissolving ovum membranes.
Tail: A long whip-like flagellum exhibiting undulating movements that generate sperm motility toward the ampulla.

Step 3: Formulating the Matched Combination
The correct functional pairings are: Head with genetic material (A-iv), Middle piece with energy (B-iii), Acrosome with enzymes (C-i), and Tail with sperm motility (D-ii).
Final Answer: A-iv, B-iii, C-i, D-ii

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q11 - Identification of human reproductive cell with haploid chromosomes

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Human somatic and germ mother cells are diploid with 46 chromosomes (23 pairs), whereas mature gametes and post-meiosis I cells are haploid containing 23 chromosomes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cell Ploidy
Spermatogonia are primitive male germ cells that undergo mitosis and are diploid with 46 chromosomes.
A zygote is produced by the syngamy of haploid sperm and ovum nuclei, restoring the diploid state of 46 chromosomes.
Oogonia are female stem germ cells that divide mitotically during fetal life and are diploid with 46 chromosomes.
A secondary oocyte is the daughter cell produced when a diploid primary oocyte (46 chromosomes) completes the first meiotic reduction division, halving the chromosomal number to 23 chromosomes.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The secondary oocyte is a haploid cell possessing exactly 23 chromosomes.
Final Answer: Secondary oöcyte

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q12 - Match embryonic development terms with their definitions

questiontext.text:
Match the following and choose the correct options:

Column IColumn II
A. Trophoblasti. Embedding of blastocyst in the endometrium
B. Cleavageii. Group of cells that would differentiate as embryo
C. Inner cell massiii. Outer layer of blastocyst attached to the endometrium
D. Implantationiv. Mitotic division of zygote

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Early mammalian development proceeds through cleavage divisions to yield a blastocyst, which attaches to and embeds into the maternal endometrium.

Step 2: Matching Analysis
Trophoblast: The outer single-layered epithelium of the blastocyst that establishes direct contact with and adheres to the uterine endometrium, corresponding to the outer layer of blastocyst attached to the endometrium.
Cleavage: Rapid, sequential mitotic divisions undergone by the unicellular zygote without intervening cell growth, corresponding to the mitotic division of zygote.
Inner cell mass: The centrally positioned pluripotential cluster of cells within the blastocyst that gives rise to all embryonic germ layers and tissues, corresponding to the group of cells that would differentiate as embryo.
Implantation: The physiological process in which the expanded blastocyst penetrates and becomes completely embedded into the vascular endometrium, corresponding to the embedding of blastocyst in the endometrium.

Step 3: Formulating the Matched Combination
The correct correspondences are: Trophoblast with the outer layer attached to endometrium (A-iii), Cleavage with mitotic division of zygote (B-iv), Inner cell mass with group of cells differentiating into embryo (C-ii), and Implantation with embedding of blastocyst (D-i).
Final Answer: A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q13 - Endocrine hormone not secreted by human placenta

questiontext.text: Which of the following hormones is not secreted by human placenta?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The placenta serves as a feto-maternal organ facilitating exchange of materials and acting as an endocrine organ that produces vital pregnancy hormones.

Step 2: Hormones Secreted by the Placenta
The human syncytiotrophoblast of the placenta synthesizes and releases protein hormones including human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), and relaxin (later in pregnancy), as well as steroid hormones including estrogens and progesterone.

Step 3: Source of Luteinizing Hormone
Luteinizing hormone (LH) is a glycoprotein gonadotropin synthesized and secreted exclusively by the anterior pituitary gland under hypothalamic stimulation by GnRH. It is not secreted by the placenta.

Step 4: Check and Final Conclusion
Among the listed hormones, luteinizing hormone is not produced by the placenta.
Final Answer: LH

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q14 - Duct formed by vas deferens and seminal vesicle

questiontext.text: The vas deferens receives duct from the seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The male excurrent duct system conveys spermatozoa from the testicle to the exterior, joining secretions from accessory glands along its course.

Step 2: Anatomical Junction and Resulting Duct
The vas deferens ascends from each testis into the pelvic cavity, loops over the ureter, and reaches the base of the urinary bladder where its terminal ampulla joins the short duct emerging from the seminal vesicle. The union of these two ducts gives rise to the ejaculatory duct. The paired ejaculatory ducts traverse through the prostate gland and empty into the prostatic urethra.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The conduit formed by the union of the vas deferens and the duct of the seminal vesicle is the ejaculatory duct.
Final Answer: Ejaculatory duct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q15 - Definition and anatomical identity of urethral meatus

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The human male urethra serves dual functions as a urinogenital duct, conducting urine from the urinary bladder and semen from the reproductive ducts.

Step 2: Definition of Urethral Meatus
Anatomically, the term 'meatus' signifies an opening, canal, or passage leading to the exterior of the body. The male urethra traverses the corpus spongiosum of the penis and terminates at its tip as a slit-like external orifice, termed the urethral meatus. Hence, it constitutes the external opening of the urinogenital duct.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The urethral meatus is defined as the external opening of the urinogenital duct.
Final Answer: External opening of the urinogenital duct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q16 - Developmental stage of morula in human embryogenesis

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Following syngamy, the single-celled zygote undergoes cleavages to produce a succession of embryonic stages characterized by increasing cell numbers and morphological changes.

Step 2: Chronological Sequence of Early Stages
The single-celled zygote undergoes mitotic divisions forming 2, 4, 8, and 16 daughter cells called blastomeres. The solid ball of 8 to 16 blastomeres resembling a mulberry is known as the morula. As division continues, fluid accumulates inside the cell mass, transforming the morula into a hollow sphere called the blastocyst. The blastocyst subsequently attaches to and embeds in the uterine wall during implantation. Therefore, the morula stage occurs specifically between the zygote and blastocyst stages.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The morula is an intermediate developmental stage positioned chronologically between the unicellular zygote and the multicellular blastocyst.
Final Answer: Between the zygote and blastocyst

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q17 - Membranous cover surrounding ovum at ovulation

questiontext.text: The membranous cover of the ovum at ovulation is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During ovulation, the Graafian follicle ruptures, releasing the secondary oocyte into the peritoneal cavity enveloped by distinct cellular and acellular layers.

Step 2: Analysis of Oocyte Coverings
The ovulated secondary oocyte is bounded internally by its plasma membrane. Immediately external to the plasma membrane is the non-cellular, glycoprotein coat called the zona pellucida. Surrounding the zona pellucida is a prominent, radiating mantle of follicle (granulosa) cells cemented together by hyaluronic acid, known as the corona radiata. This outer cellular mantle functions as the membranous protective cover of the ovulated egg.
The chorion, in contrast, is an extra-embryonic membrane that develops much later during embryogenesis from the trophoblast and somatic mesoderm.

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
The protective membranous covering encasing the ovulated ovum is the corona radiata.
Final Answer: Corona radiata

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q18 - Odd structure among parts of female reproductive system

questiontext.text: Identify the odd one from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The female reproductive system comprises internal genital organs (ovaries, fallopian tubes, uterus, and vagina) and external genitalia (vulva).

Step 2: Anatomical Classification of Listed Parts
The Fallopian tube (oviduct) consists of three contiguous anatomical segments: the funnel-shaped infundibulum bearing finger-like projections called fimbriae, the wide ampulla, and the narrow isthmus connecting to the uterus. Hence, fimbriae, infundibulum, and isthmus are integral sub-parts of the internal accessory duct system (oviduct).
In contrast, the labia minora are paired, slender folds of mucous membrane located beneath the labia majora that form part of the external genitalia (vulva).

Step 3: Check and Final Conclusion
Because fimbriae, infundibulum, and isthmus are anatomical components of the Fallopian tube while the labia minora are part of the external genitalia, labia minora is the odd structure.
Final Answer: Labia minora
